O.outcome_detail: perceived clarity about whether one's GenAI use complies with institutional rules

cells.quote: A closer examination of the heatmap shows that students who reported being unfamiliar with institutional regulations are strongly concentrated in theI do not knowcategory. This indicates that a lack of awareness of institutional rules is closely associated with uncertainty regarding acceptable use. However, the results also show that even among students who reported awareness of institutional regulations, certainty about rule-compliant behavior remains limited.
cells.note: The study reports an exploratory cross-tabulation/heatmap rather than an inferential effect size; awareness is associated with greater clarity relative to unfamiliarity, but does not eliminate uncertainty.

D.treatment: awareness visualization of group members’ task perceptions

O.outcome_detail: perceived planning problems and encountered challenges

cells.quote: The study showed that without these kinds of visualizations, individuals rated planning as more problematic, and they encountered more challenges. Consequently, they saw a high need for planning strategies and expected them to be more effective than teamwork strategies. This was different for the groups with visualizations. This group reported higher levels of success with their strategies and it expected both planning and teamwork strategies to be equally effective.
cells.note: The study text does not state participants’ age, prior knowledge, duration, or assignment method. The setting is coded as online-self-paced because the study concerns online collaboration, although instructor involvement is not specified.

O.outcome_detail: speech-in-noise perception measured by speech reception threshold

result.effect: SNR decreased by 0.35 dB on average

cells.quote: On average, participants SNR decreased by 0.35 dB after either short-term training compared to before (a decreased SNR is re ﬂecting an improved speech perception in noise, since speech is perceived despite increasing noise).
cells.note: Both training sessions were approximately 42 minutes and speech-in-noise perception was measured before and after each session.

result.effect: IMpost – IMpre: Δβ = −0.592, p < 0.001; AUpost – AUpre: Δβ = −0.118, p = 0.817; interaction Δχ²(1) = 6.111, p = 0.013

cells.quote: Post-hoc comparisons revealed that SNR signi ﬁcantly improved, but only after the immersive training session (IMpost – IMpre: Δβ = −0.592, SE = 0.135,t = −4.395, p < 0.001, see Fig. 2B), while no signiﬁcant change in SNR was observed after the auditory training session (AU post – AUpre: Δβ = −0.118, SE = 0.135,t = -0.875, p = 0.817, see Fig. 2A).
cells.note: The cross-over design was counterbalanced across participants.

D.comparison: auditory training in participants with lower auditory working memory

result.effect: ChangeAU – ChangeIM: Δβ = −0.677, SE = 0.148, t = −4.561, p < 0.001

cells.quote: In contrast, a participant with lower AWM capacity (i.e., 1 SD below the mean) experienced a signiﬁcantly greater improvement in SNR f ollowing the immersive training compared to the auditory training (AWM 1 SD below average: ChangeAU– ChangeIM:Δβ = −0.677, SE = 0.148,t = −4.561, p < 0.001).
cells.note: AWM was treated as a continuous moderator; the comparison describes a hypothetical participant at 1 SD below the mean, not grouped participants.

D.comparison: auditory training in participants with higher hearing loss

result.effect: ChangeAU – ChangeIM: Δβ = −0.729, SE = 0.163, t = −4.481, p < 0.001

cells.quote: Post-hoc analyses showed that in participants with higher PTA (i.e., PTA 1 SD above the mean), the training-induced change was signiﬁcantly greater for immersive training compared to auditory training (PTA 1 SD above average: ChangeAU – ChangeIM: Δβ = −0.729, SE = 0.163,t = −4.481, p < 0.001).
cells.note: PTA indexed hearing loss; the higher-PTA comparison was defined as 1 SD above the mean.
